help.elections.title: Elections
help.elections.summary: How an election runs on its own dates, who is entitled to take part, and how to nominate, accept and vote.
help.elections.what-it-is.heading: What this screen is
help.elections.what-it-is.b0: Every election your part of the family is holding. **Active** is anything not yet finished — one that has not opened, one taking nominations, one waiting for its ballot to open, and one being voted in. **Past** is the ones that have closed.
help.elections.what-it-is.b1: Elections that have not been published yet are not listed. An organizer writes an election as a draft first, and a draft is not a ballot.
help.elections.what-it-is.b2: Open one to see its positions, its two date windows, and whatever you can do in it today.
help.elections.the-dates.heading: The dates run it
help.elections.the-dates.b0: An election has two windows, and nobody presses anything to move it between them.
help.elections.the-dates.b1.i0.text: From the day they open to the day they close. Put yourself forward, or put somebody else forward.
help.elections.the-dates.b1.i1.text: From the day it opens to the day it closes. Cast a vote, or change one.
help.elections.the-dates.b2: **Both ends count.** An election whose nominations read "January 1st – January 5th" is open on the 5th, right up to the end of the day. The same is true of voting — with one exception, below.
help.elections.the-dates.b3: Voting never opens before nominations close, so the list of candidates you are voting on cannot change under you. There is often a gap in between, and the screen says what it is waiting for.
help.elections.the-dates.b4: **Voting may open on the same day nominations close, and then that day belongs to voting.** Nominations run through their closing date, or until voting opens, whichever comes first — so on a shared day the nomination form is already shut and the ballot is live. If your family wants the whole of that day for nominations, the closing date goes one day earlier.
help.elections.the-dates.b5: Nothing here happens at a time of day. A window opens on its date and closes at the end of its closing date, and the screen shows the same dates to everybody.
help.elections.the-dates.b6: **"The end of the day" means the end of the day where your family is.** An election records the timezone it was scheduled in, and both the dates on screen and the moment the ballot actually shuts are read in that one timezone — so a relative in another part of the world sees the same closing date as everybody else, and the ballot stays open until your family's midnight rather than somebody else's.
help.elections.who-votes.heading: Who an election is for
help.elections.who-votes.b0: An election belongs to one level of the family, and the screen names it under the title.
help.elections.who-votes.b1.i0.text: The whole family. Everybody can see it, be nominated, and vote.
help.elections.who-votes.b1.i1.text: Only members whose chapter is in that region.
help.elections.who-votes.b2: The levels do not mix. A chapter election is invisible to the rest of the family — it is not listed, and its link does not open — and it can only fill offices the family records at chapter level. See [Regions & chapters](/help/regions-and-chapters) for how the family is divided up, and [Board positions](/help/board-positions) for the offices themselves.
help.elections.who-votes.b3: **If you are not in a chapter, you are under National.** You see national elections and take part in them, and regional and chapter elections are not yours. Your chapter is on [My Profile](/personal-info) — an administrator can also set it for you.
help.elections.nominating.heading: Nominating somebody
help.elections.nominating.b0: While nominations are open, the election lists every office on the ballot, and under each one the people who have been nominated for it. Any member may nominate.
help.elections.nominating.b1.i0: Find the office you want to nominate for and press **Nominate** beside it.
help.elections.nominating.b1.i1: To stand yourself, press **Put myself forward**. You are on the ballot straight away — nobody has to accept their own nomination.
help.elections.nominating.b1.i2: To put somebody else forward, find them in **Who are you nominating?** and press **Nominate**.
help.elections.nominating.b2: The name box searches any part of any name, so typing "allen" finds Martha Allen. It lists only the people this election is for, which is why a chapter election offers fewer names than the family has.
help.elections.nominating.b3: **Several members can nominate the same person for the same office.** They appear once on the list, and it says how many people put them forward — "nominated by you and 2 others". A second nomination is not a duplicate; it is another member saying they want them.
help.elections.nominating.b4: One person can be nominated once per office by you, and can be nominated for as many offices as you like.
help.elections.withdrawing.heading: Taking a nomination back
help.elections.withdrawing.b0: A nomination you made shows **Take my name off** beside it, and one you made for yourself shows **Withdraw**. Either way you are only ever removing your own name.
help.elections.withdrawing.b1: **If other members nominated the same person, they stay on the ballot.** Only your name comes off, and the count beside them goes down by one. If you were the only person who nominated them, they come off the ballot altogether — the screen says which of the two is about to happen before you confirm.
help.elections.withdrawing.b2: Two things stop it, and both are about not changing a ballot under the people reading it:
help.elections.withdrawing.b3.i0.text: An accepted nomination stays on the ballot. The way off it is for them to decline — see Accepting or declining below. The exception is your own: you can always withdraw yourself.
help.elections.withdrawing.b3.i1.text: Once the window is over, nothing comes off the ballot. Declining is the only way out from then on.
help.elections.withdrawing.b4: You cannot take somebody else’s nomination off, even if you are an administrator of the family. A nomination is a thing one member said, and only they can unsay it.
help.elections.accepting.heading: Accepting or declining
help.elections.accepting.b0: If somebody nominates you, the election opens with **You have been nominated!** at the top, one row per office. **Accept** puts you on the ballot; **Decline** takes you off it.
help.elections.accepting.b1: It cannot be changed afterwards, so the screen asks you to confirm. Only nominations you have accepted appear as candidates when voting opens — a nomination nobody answered is not on the ballot.
help.elections.accepting.b2: You can still answer after nominations close. The window governs who may be nominated, not how long you have to reply.
help.elections.voting.heading: Voting
help.elections.voting.b0: While voting is open, each office lists the candidates who accepted. Press one, confirm, and your vote is recorded.
help.elections.voting.b1: You may change your vote as often as you like until the window closes — pressing another candidate replaces your earlier vote rather than adding to it. One vote per office.
help.elections.voting.b2: **Your ballot is yours.** You can see your own votes and nobody else can, and nothing anywhere shows another member who they voted for.
help.elections.results.heading: Results
help.elections.results.b0: Once the voting window has closed, **Results** appears at the foot of the election with the vote count for each candidate, ordered by count, as many rows deep as the office has winners.
help.elections.results.b1: Nothing is published while voting is still open, and nothing has to be pressed to publish it — the day after voting closes, the results are there.
